```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Run the network to steady state with no drug (the authors equilibrated for
# 20 days before any treatment) and return the final state vector, to be
# passed as `inits =` to the treatment solve.
equilibrate <- function(mod, params = NULL, inits = NULL, days = 20) {
  eq <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod,
    rxode2::et(c(0, days * 1440)),
    params = params,
    inits = inits,
    returnType = "data.frame",
    maxsteps = 1e6
  )
  unlist(eq[nrow(eq), mod$state])
}

# Relative dose (Figure 5 y-axis) to absolute dose: D = LB + r * (UB - LB)
rel_to_abs <- function(r, lb, ub) lb + r * (ub - lb)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhang_2014_sunitinib_vegfr_qsp"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhang_2014_sunitinib_vegfr_qsp"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/psp.2013.65> (open access, PMC3910016)

Zhang, Birtwistle and Gallo built a mechanistic "enhanced pharmacodynamic"
(ePD) model of VEGFR2 signaling, linked it to the plasma PK of sunitinib, ran a
Sobol global sensitivity analysis to pick further drug targets (VEGF, PI3K,
PLC-gamma, MEK), and then used day-by-day genetic-algorithm optimisation to
design 28-day five-drug regimens that held active ERK (pERK) and active Akt
(pAkt) at or below 20% of their pre-treatment steady state. The packaged model
is the full five-drug PK/ePD system the optimiser drove (the authors'
`VEGFRModelDrugs.m`). The sensitivity analysis and the optimiser itself are
analyses run on the model and are not part of it.

# Population

There are no fitted subjects. The network represents a generic VEGFR2-driven
solid tumor (20 mL, half cells by volume) with literature-derived kinetic
constants and protein abundances (Supplementary Tables S1 and S2). The drug PK
are human typical values: sunitinib (Houk 2009) and bevacizumab (Li 2013) from
published population PK models, and buparlisib (BKM120) and selumetinib
(AZD6244) from two-compartment fits by the authors to digitised mean plasma
profiles (Bendell 2012; O'Neil 2011). The PLC-gamma inhibitor is hypothetical.
Three mutation scenarios are simulated by changing protein levels or activity:
NF1 loss (100-fold under-expression), an activating PI3K mutation (threefold
catalytic activity) and PTEN loss (100-fold under-expression).

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhang_2014_sunitinib_vegfr_qsp"))$population)
```

# Source trace

The paper's printed tables (Supplementary Tables S1-S4) and the authors'
published MATLAB code (Supplementary Data: `VEGFRModelDrugs.m`,
`GetInitialConditions.m` and the parameter file `physiosetbasis.mat`) are both
available. Where they disagree the code is used, because it is what produced
the published figures (see "Code versus Table S1" below, which shows that the
Table S1 values do not reproduce Figure 3). Every `ini()` value carries its
source in an in-file comment; the table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Reaction rates `v1f` ... `v76`, ODEs for the 43 signaling species | n/a | `VEGFRModelDrugs.m` reaction and ODE blocks; Table S1 (reactions 1-36), Table S2 (ODEs), Table S3 (drug mechanisms) |
| `lk1f` ... `lkh`, `n_fb` (69 network constants) | see model file | `physiosetbasis.mat` row 1, k(1)-k(77); Table S1 |
| `lk4`, `lkm4`, `lk5`, `lkm5` (k(7)-k(10)) | not used | Code sets the PLC-gamma phosphorylation rates `v4f1`, `v4r1` to 0, so these never enter the ODEs and the always-zero `PLCgP` state is omitted |
| `shp1`, `pten`, `pp2a`, `nf1` | 100, 100, 20, 25 nM | `VEGFRModelDrugs.m`; Table S1 reactions 7, 9, 12, 29 |
| `f_cell` (Vc/Ve = 1) | 0.5 | `VEGFRModelDrugs.m` `f = 0.5`; Table S1 note |
| Initial conditions | see model file | `GetInitialConditions.m` (PDK1 100.534 nM); Table S2 |
| Sunitinib `lka`, `lcl`, `lvc`, `lq`, `lvp`, `lfdepot` | 0.0033 1/min, 0.863 L/min, 2030 L, 0.120 L/min, 583 L, 0.95 | `VEGFRModelDrugs.m`; Table S4 |
| Sunitinib `lkon`, `lkoff` | 1 1/(nM min), 10 1/min | `VEGFRModelDrugs.m`; Table S3 |
| Bevacizumab CL, Vc, Q, Vp | 0.00016 L/min, 2.83 L, 0.0004416 L/min, 2.49 L | `VEGFRModelDrugs.m`; Table S4 |
| Bevacizumab `lkon_bevacizumab`, `lkoff_bevacizumab` | 0.0021 1/(nM min), 0.00378 1/min | `VEGFRModelDrugs.m`; Table S3 |
| Buparlisib ka, CL, Vc, Q, Vp, Ki | 0.0136 1/min, 0.0144 L/min, 43.1 L, 0.711 L/min, 899.95 L, 30 nM | `VEGFRModelDrugs.m`; Tables S4 and S3 |
| Selumetinib ka, CL, Vc, Q, Vp, Ki | 0.022 1/min, 0.4084 L/min, 136.13 L, 0.1134 L/min, 30.9 L, 14 nM | `VEGFRModelDrugs.m`; Tables S4 and S3 |
| PLC-gamma inhibitor kel, Ki | 0.000963 1/min, 1000 nM | `VEGFRModelDrugs.m` |
| Dose conversions (mg to nmol) | 50 mg sunitinib = 1.25e5 nmol; 350 mg bevacizumab = 78.33 nmol/min for 30 min; 100 mg buparlisib = 243900 nmol; 50-100 mg selumetinib = 109242-218484 nmol | `FigS1A_*PK.m` scripts; `FigS3.m` optimiser bounds; Table 1 |

# Equilibrating the network

The packaged initial conditions are the authors' pre-equilibration values. As
in the paper, every simulation first runs the drug-free network for 20 days and
then starts treatment from that steady state.

```{r equilibrate}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhang_2014_sunitinib_vegfr_qsp"))
ss_base <- equilibrate(mod)

# The steady state must be a true steady state: one more day changes nothing.
ss_check <- equilibrate(mod, inits = ss_base, days = 1)
stopifnot(
  abs(ss_check[["erk_p"]] / ss_base[["erk_p"]] - 1) < 1e-4,
  abs(ss_check[["pip3_akt_p"]] / ss_base[["pip3_akt_p"]] - 1) < 1e-4
)

tibble(
  Species = c("pERK (erk_p)", "pAkt (pip3_akt_p)", "free VEGFR2 (vr)", "free VEGF (vegf)"),
  `Steady state (nM)` = signif(ss_base[c("erk_p", "pip3_akt_p", "vr", "vegf")], 4)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Drug-free steady state of the base network.")
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 3a: VEGF stimulation in vitro

For Figure 3a the authors used a separate in vitro version of the network
(`InVitro.m`) in which the ligand concentration is held constant: the network is
equilibrated with no VEGF (serum starvation, 7 days), then VEGF is set to a
constant 0.5 nM. The same structure is obtained here by replacing the VEGF ODE
with `d/dt(vegf) <- 0`. (`InVitro.m` starts PDK1 at 100 nM rather than 100.534
nM; the difference changes pAkt by less than 0.1 nM.)

```{r figure-3a}
mod_invitro <- suppressMessages(mod |> rxode2::model(d/dt(vegf) <- 0))
ss_starved <- equilibrate(mod_invitro, inits = c(vegf = 0), days = 7)
ss_starved[["vegf"]] <- 0.5
fig3a <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_invitro,
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 180, by = 1)),
  inits = ss_starved,
  returnType = "data.frame"
)

fig3a |>
  select(time, pERK, pAkt) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "output", values_to = "conc") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 60, conc)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~output, scales = "free_y") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (hours)", y = "Concentration (nM)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3a of Zhang 2014 (0.5 nM VEGF, constant)."
  )
```

Figure 3a shows pERK rising to a plateau of about 395 nM within 15 minutes, and
pAkt peaking at about 92 nM and then declining to about 82 nM at 3 hours.

```{r figure-3a-check}
fig3a_check <- c(
  perk_plateau = fig3a$pERK[fig3a$time == 180],
  pakt_peak = max(fig3a$pAkt),
  pakt_3h = fig3a$pAkt[fig3a$time == 180]
)
fig3a_check
stopifnot(
  abs(fig3a_check[["perk_plateau"]] / 395 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(fig3a_check[["pakt_peak"]] / 92 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(fig3a_check[["pakt_3h"]] / 82 - 1) < 0.05
)
```

## Figure 3b: single 50 mg dose of sunitinib

```{r figure-3b}
ev_sun <- rxode2::et(amt = 1.25e5, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 10 * 1440, by = 10))
fig3b <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_sun, inits = ss_base, returnType = "data.frame")

# Phosphorylated receptor: the free dimer and the dimer with each bound adaptor
p_receptor <- c("vegf_vr2_p", "vegf_vr2_p_pi3k", "vegf_vr2_p_plcg", "vegf_vr2_p_grb2sos")
fig3b <- fig3b |>
  mutate(
    pERK_pct = 100 * pERK / ss_base[["erk_p"]],
    pAkt_pct = 100 * pAkt / ss_base[["pip3_akt_p"]],
    pR_free_pct = 100 * vegf_vr2_p / ss_base[["vegf_vr2_p"]]
  )

fig3b |>
  select(time, pERK = pERK_pct, pAkt = pAkt_pct) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "output", values_to = "pct") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 1440, pct)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~output) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Percent of baseline",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3b of Zhang 2014 (single 50 mg oral dose of sunitinib)."
  )
```

The text reports a sunitinib Cmax of 42 nM and nadirs of about 45% for pAkt and
pERK, and Figure 3b places the pERK nadir (about 46%) near day 2.3 and the pAkt
nadir (about 47%) near day 1.7, with both back to about 97-98% at day 10. The
text also says sunitinib "inhibited VEGFR phosphorylation by 27%"; the free
phosphorylated dimer falls to 27% of baseline at its nadir, so the printed 27%
is read here as the nadir level.

```{r figure-3b-check}
fig3b_check <- tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "Sunitinib Cmax (nM)", "pERK nadir (% of baseline)", "pERK nadir time (day)",
    "pAkt nadir (% of baseline)", "pAkt nadir time (day)",
    "Free phosphorylated receptor nadir (% of baseline)",
    "pERK at day 10 (%)", "pAkt at day 10 (%)"
  ),
  Paper = c(42, 46, 2.3, 47, 1.7, 27, 98, 97),
  Simulated = c(
    max(fig3b$Cc),
    min(fig3b$pERK_pct), fig3b$time[which.min(fig3b$pERK_pct)] / 1440,
    min(fig3b$pAkt_pct), fig3b$time[which.min(fig3b$pAkt_pct)] / 1440,
    min(fig3b$pR_free_pct),
    fig3b$pERK_pct[fig3b$time == 10 * 1440], fig3b$pAkt_pct[fig3b$time == 10 * 1440]
  )
)
fig3b_check |>
  mutate(Simulated = signif(Simulated, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Figure 3b and text values (paper values read from the figure except Cmax and the 27%).")
stopifnot(all(abs(fig3b_check$Simulated / fig3b_check$Paper - 1) < 0.1))
```

## Figure S1: single-dose plasma PK of each drug

The authors' Figure S1 scripts use sunitinib 50 mg, bevacizumab 350 mg over 30
minutes, buparlisib 100 mg, selumetinib 218,484 nmol (100 mg; the script
comment says 50 mg, but 2.19e5 nmol is the 100 mg upper bound of Table 1) and a
PLC-gamma inhibitor starting at 10 umol/L.

```{r figure-s1}
dose_tbl <- tibble(
  drug = c("sunitinib", "bevacizumab", "buparlisib", "selumetinib", "PLC-gamma inhibitor"),
  cmt = c("depot", "central_bevacizumab", "depot_buparlisib", "depot_selumetinib", "central_plcginhibitor"),
  amt = c(1.25e5, 78.33 * 30, 243900, 218484, 10000),
  rate = c(0, 78.33, 0, 0, 0),
  out = c("Cc", "Cc_bevacizumab", "Cc_buparlisib", "Cc_selumetinib", "Cc_plcginhibitor")
)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 4 * 1440, by = 10), 30)))

pk_one <- function(i) {
  d <- dose_tbl[i, ]
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = d$amt, rate = d$rate, cmt = d$cmt) |> rxode2::et(obs_times)
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, inits = ss_base, returnType = "data.frame")
  tibble(drug = d$drug, time = s$time, Cc = s[[d$out]])
}
pk_s1 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(dose_tbl)), pk_one))

ggplot(pk_s1, aes(time / 1440, Cc)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~drug, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Plasma concentration (nM)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure S1B of Zhang 2014 (single standard doses)."
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

Single-dose NCA for each drug's plasma concentration, grouped by drug. The paper
reports only the sunitinib Cmax (42 nM), which is compared below.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- pk_s1 |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(id = 1L, treatment = drug) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(treatment, time)

dose_df <- dose_tbl |>
  transmute(id = 1L, treatment = drug, time = 0, amt = amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 4 * 1440, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  mutate(tmax = tmax / 60) |>
  rename(
    "Drug" = treatment,
    "Cmax (nM)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-4d (nM*min)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Simulated single-dose NCA by drug.")
```

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax,
  "sunitinib", 42
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  params = "cmax",
  units = c(cmax = "nM"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published sunitinib Cmax after 50 mg. * differs by >20%.")
```

# Mutation scenarios and Figure 5e/f

The mutations change protein levels or activity in the network. Each
scenario is re-equilibrated before treatment, and pERK and pAkt are expressed
relative to that scenario's own drug-free steady state (as in the authors'
optimiser).

```{r mutations}
scenarios <- list(
  "Base network" = NULL,
  "NF1 loss (100-fold)" = c(nf1 = 0.25),
  "PI3K activating (3x k8)" = c(lk8 = log(3 * 1500)),
  "PTEN loss (100-fold)" = c(pten = 1)
)
ss_mut <- lapply(scenarios, function(p) equilibrate(mod, params = p))
tibble(
  Scenario = names(ss_mut),
  `pERK (nM)` = vapply(ss_mut, function(s) s[["erk_p"]], numeric(1)),
  `pAkt (nM)` = vapply(ss_mut, function(s) s[["pip3_akt_p"]], numeric(1))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Drug-free steady state by mutation scenario.")
```

Figure 5e shows the regimen the optimiser chose for the PTEN-loss network, and
Figure 5f the response. The relative doses below were read from Figure 5e by
the maintainers (relative dose r gives dose LB + r x (UB - LB), Table 1 bounds
in nmol): sunitinib every day; bevacizumab (near the upper bound) and
buparlisib on day 1; buparlisib again on days 2 and 27; selumetinib on day 1,
taken twice 12 hours apart. Days are counted from 1 at time 0.

```{r figure-5ef}
sun_rel <- c(
  0.95, 0.54, 0.31, 0.42, 0.75, 0.08, 0.50, 0.30, 0.38, 0.49, 0.33, 0.40, 0.45, 0.51,
  0.51, 0.32, 0.42, 0.51, 0.45, 0.56, 0.33, 0.49, 0.44, 0.44, 0.47, 0.57, 0.02, 0.52
)
bev_rate <- rel_to_abs(0.98, 78.3, 234.9)
ev_pten <- rxode2::et(
  amt = rel_to_abs(sun_rel, 25094, 250940),
  time = (seq_along(sun_rel) - 1) * 1440,
  cmt = "depot"
) |>
  rxode2::et(amt = bev_rate * 30, rate = bev_rate, time = 0, cmt = "central_bevacizumab") |>
  rxode2::et(
    amt = rel_to_abs(c(0.98, 0.37, 0.08), 121832, 243665),
    time = c(0, 1, 26) * 1440,
    cmt = "depot_buparlisib"
  ) |>
  rxode2::et(amt = rel_to_abs(0.55, 109242, 218484), time = c(0, 720), cmt = "depot_selumetinib") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 28 * 1440, by = 30))

ss_pten <- ss_mut[["PTEN loss (100-fold)"]]
fig5f <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_pten, params = c(pten = 1), inits = ss_pten, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(
    day = time / 1440,
    pERK_frac = pERK / ss_pten[["erk_p"]],
    pAkt_frac = pAkt / ss_pten[["pip3_akt_p"]]
  )

fig5f |>
  select(day, pERK = pERK_frac, pAkt = pAkt_frac) |>
  pivot_longer(-day, names_to = "output", values_to = "frac") |>
  ggplot(aes(day, frac, colour = output)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(pERK = "black", pAkt = "red")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Fractional response", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5f of Zhang 2014 (PTEN-loss network, regimen of Figure 5e)."
  )
```

Figure 5f shows pAkt rising to about 0.7 in the first half-day, falling to about
0.2 by day 3 and staying near 0.2 for the rest of the cycle, with a dip near
day 26; pERK rises to about 0.17 around day 2-3 and then settles near 0.1.

```{r figure-5f-check}
pakt_early_peak <- max(fig5f$pAkt_frac[fig5f$day > 0.1 & fig5f$day < 1])
pakt_late <- fig5f$pAkt_frac[fig5f$day >= 3]
perk_late <- fig5f$pERK_frac[fig5f$day >= 5]
c(
  pakt_early_peak = pakt_early_peak,
  pakt_median_after_day3 = median(pakt_late),
  pakt_q90_after_day3 = unname(quantile(pakt_late, 0.9)),
  perk_median_after_day5 = median(perk_late)
)
stopifnot(
  abs(pakt_early_peak - 0.7) < 0.1,
  abs(median(pakt_late) - 0.19) < 0.03,
  quantile(pakt_late, 0.9) < 0.22,
  median(perk_late) < 0.15
)
```

# Code versus Table S1

Ten values in the printed Table S1 differ from the parameter file the authors
ran (`physiosetbasis.mat`). With the Table S1 values the drug-free network
carries almost no active Akt and sunitinib does not reduce pERK, so Figure 3b
cannot be reproduced; with the code's values it is reproduced (above). The
model therefore uses the code's values.

```{r table-s1}
table_s1 <- c(
  lkmpg = log(2000), lk6r = log(10), lk11f = log(0.18), lkm12 = log(0.99),
  lkm13 = log(0.1), lk16f = log(0.18), lvm18 = log(18), lkm28 = log(2.56),
  lk29 = log(0.01), lkm32 = log(2400)
)
ss_tab <- equilibrate(mod, params = table_s1)
sim_tab <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_sun, params = table_s1, inits = ss_tab, returnType = "data.frame")
tibble(
  `Parameter set` = c("Code (packaged)", "Table S1 as printed"),
  `Baseline pAkt (nM)` = c(ss_base[["pip3_akt_p"]], ss_tab[["pip3_akt_p"]]),
  `pERK nadir after 50 mg (%)` = c(min(fig3b$pERK_pct), 100 * min(sim_tab$pERK) / ss_tab[["erk_p"]]),
  `pAkt nadir after 50 mg (%)` = c(min(fig3b$pAkt_pct), 100 * min(sim_tab$pAkt) / ss_tab[["pip3_akt_p"]])
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Figure 3b under the two parameter sets.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Differences between Table S1 and the authors' code.** The code's parameter
  file is used for every value. The printed Table S1 differs for Kmpg (code
  500 nM; table 2.0e3), k6r (0.2; 1.0e1 1/min), k11f (17.9; 1.8e-1
  1/(nM min)), Km12 (100; 0.99 nM), Km13 (100; 0.1 nM), k16f (17.9; 1.8e-1
  1/(nM min)), Vm18 (60.3; 1.8e1 nM/min), Km28 (200; 2.56 nM), k29 (130;
  1.0e-2 1/min) and Km32 (2000; 2.4e3 nM). The Hill coefficient of the pAkt
  feedback (n = 3) is printed in Table S1 without a value and is taken from the
  code. The section above shows that only the code's values reproduce Figure 3.
- **Differences between Table S4 and the code.** Selumetinib Vp is 30.9 L in
  the code and 32.09 L in Table S4; the code's value is used. Bevacizumab
  clearance is 0.00016 L/min in both the model code and Table S4; the
  stand-alone Figure S1 script uses 0.00015 L/min, which is not used here.
- **Initial conditions.** The full drug model (`GetInitialConditions.m`) starts
  PDK1 at 100.534 nM; the sunitinib-only and in vitro scripts use 100 nM. The
  full-model value is used. Only conserved totals (each kinase or adaptor plus
  its complexes) survive equilibration, and this difference moves steady-state
  pAkt by less than 0.1 nM.
- **Omitted bookkeeping.** The always-zero `PLCgP` state and its unused rate
  constants (k4, Km4, k5, Km5), the two running-integral states the authors
  used for the sensitivity analysis (area between the baseline and effect
  curves of pERK and pAkt), and the unused bevacizumab infusion-rate state are
  not carried. Bevacizumab is dosed as an ordinary 30-minute infusion
  (`rate =`) into `central_bevacizumab`.
- **PLC-gamma inhibitor dose units.** The authors set the inhibitor's plasma
  concentration directly (2-10 umol/L, Table 1), so `central_plcginhibitor` is
  a concentration state in nM and its dose `amt` is in nmol/L, unlike the
  other drugs (nmol).
- **Optimiser day resets.** The authors' optimiser restarted each day by
  overwriting every drug's input state with that day's dose (zero if not
  dosed). For the oral depots this discards less than 1% of a dose, but for the
  PLC-gamma inhibitor (half-life about 12 hours) it discards about a quarter of
  the previous day's concentration. The packaged model accumulates doses
  normally, so regimens containing the PLC-gamma inhibitor will not match the
  optimiser's internal simulations exactly. The Figure 5e/f check above uses
  the PTEN-loss regimen, which has no PLC-gamma inhibitor.
- **Figure 5e doses** were read from the published figure by the maintainers
  and are approximate (about +/- 0.02 relative dose).
- **Time units.** The model keeps the authors' minutes; doses are in nmol and
  concentrations in nM.
- **Mutations** are applied through `params =`: NF1 loss `nf1 = 0.25`, PTEN
  loss `pten = 1` (each 100-fold under-expression), PI3K activation
  `lk8 = log(4500)` (threefold catalytic activity). The paper does not say
  which constant carries the threefold PI3K activity; k8 (the PI3K-catalysed
  PIP2 phosphorylation rate) is the catalytic step, so it is used here.
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article (checked on
  2026-11-20).
